candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Unit and integration tests on feature/issue-790; the hourly reconcile itself is exercised only by Celery Beat at the top of the hour on the deployed release

journeys.name: medallion-writes-stay-durable-and-get-faster
assertions: bronze, silver and gold rows written by a reconcile run are readable from a new session, preserving the #752 durability guarantee
the silver stage issues a bounded number of database round trips for N bronze rows rather than one per row
per-stage commit semantics are explicit: a gold-stage failure leaves bronze and silver durably committed
GET /v1/demo/analytics continues to serve the five ADR-049 payload.kpis keys with unchanged shape
wall-clock for a 1000-row reconcile is materially below the 2244.9s production baseline

migrationCompatibility.notes: No schema change. This alters transaction boundaries and batching inside the bronze -> silver -> gold write path only. Stable and candidate read and write the same tables with the same columns, so both can run against one database during cutover.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. The hourly reconcile continues to take ~37 minutes per run, occupying a Celery fork for 62% of every hour — the current production state, degraded but not data-losing.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Roll back to the previous release. Because per-stage commits replace a single end-of-run commit, a mid-run failure after rollback may leave bronze and silver committed without a gold envelope; the next hourly run recomputes gold from silver, so the state is self-healing and no manual repair is required.

acceptanceCommands: python -m pytest tests/unit -q -k 'reconcile or shared_compute or silver or orchestrator'
doNotInfer: this changes which rows the reconcile fetches — the #744 page cap still bounds bronze at 20 pages, and GMV remains computed over that capped set
this makes ctor or live_hours available — those are hardcoded unavailable and are addressed in #789
this alters the ADR-049 five-KPI contract or the envelope payload shape
this removes the single-writer ownership model — repositories continue to flush, and only the session owner commits
